q: The Lempel–Ziv algorithm achieves optimal compression for stationary ergodic sources because:
opts: It uses the entropy H of the source explicitly
The number of LZ phrases c_n(ω) satisfies c_n/( n/log n) → h_μ(f) a.e., giving a universal entropy estimator
It is faster than Huffman coding
It uses a fixed codebook independent of the source
exp: LZ parsing into novel phrases gives c_n ≈ nh/log n phrases (SMB theorem). Each phrase needs ≈log c_n bits → total bits ≈ n·h. LZ is universal: it achieves the entropy rate h for any stationary ergodic source without knowing h in advance.
